transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-05 16:00 PT | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood SE), Ari (SparrowTech H of ML), Lena (Product), Tariq (Security), Samir (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: All right, hey everyone thanks for making time. I'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, this is Priya and Marta from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Ari: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to nail down the POC scope.
[00:11] Lena: Same here. We want to make sure we pick the right open models for our multilingual support and doc extraction.
[00:17] Jordan: Great, high level agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist models and tradeoffs, bench plan, timeline and security items. Sound right?
[00:24] Tariq: Yep, please include our SOC2 needs and key management questions.
[00:28] Priya: Quick intro from us — we'll propose a few open model variants (smaller quantized variants for low-latency chat and larger instruction models for extraction) and a bench plan that covers translation, extraction and summarization.
[00:38] Marta: Also will show how routing and fallback looks if a model misses throughput.

[00:45] Jordan: Ari can you walk us through what success looks like for SparrowTech? what metrics do we need to hit?
[00:49] Ari: Sure. Primary use case is customer support — multilingual chat (EN/ES/DE/JA), and automated invoice/contract extraction for downstream workflows. Success criteria: 1) latency under 400ms p50 for chat at 95% of requests, 2) extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our labeled set, 3) translation BLEU-ish equivalent we use internally, target reasonable human parity, and 4) cost target: keep inference spend under $0.02 per end-user session on average. Also runway to scale to 50 concurrent agents during peak.
[01:31] Jordan: Helpful — that gives us perf and cost levers. Priya, sizing notes?
[01:35] Priya: From infra notes Samir sent, average session length is ~175 tokens (roundtrip) for chat, peaks up to 750 tokens. Extraction requests average 700 tokens with long context up to 3k tokens per doc. Expected steady state throughput 25 reqs/s, peak 60 reqs/s.
[01:51] Samir (background): yeah those numbers are right, storage and data residency are the bigger constraints for us.

[01:58] Lena: On quality, we care more about extraction accuracy for legally-sensitive fields in contracts than tiny gains in chat fluency. So extraction model must prioritize precision on entity boundaries.
[02:10] Priya: Good, that suggests we should pair a stronger instruction-tuned open model for extraction and a faster quantized chat model for session routing.

[02:20] Jordan: Let's go through candidate models — note some names may be off in my notes, transcriptionwise. We'll shortlist 4-5 families:
[02:26] Priya: Candidate A: Llama3 13B instruct (or similar community Llama-variant) — strong instruction-following, can be quantized to 4-bit for cost savings but might lose edge-case extraction exactness.
[02:40] Priya: Candidate B: Mistral v2 / Mistral-instruct 7B — good micro-architecture, lower cost, fast, slightly less extractive precision on long documents.
[02:52] Priya: Candidate C: Falcon 40B instruct (or Fal-con family) — higher quality on instructions, heavier compute, needs multi-GPU for low-latency at scale.
[03:02] Priya: Candidate D: A polyglot translation-specialist (we called it Polyglot-XL in notes) — intended for EN/ES/DE/JA translation; smaller footprint but domain shift risk.
[03:12] Marta: And Candidate E: smaller distilled models for chat routing — e.g., 3-7B quantized for <200ms p50, used as front-door to route to extraction model when needed.

[03:24] Ari: Quick Q: do you have benchmarks on extraction F1 for these models on legal-ish contracts?
[03:29] Priya: We have internal benchmarks but domain shift matters; our plan is to run a 2-week bench with your sample dataset. We'll measure F1, precision, recall, latency distribution, token costs. We'll also run multilingual translation scoring — note that some translation models are specialist and outperform generalists for JA/DE.

[03:50] Jordan: On deployment mode: are you leaning hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC?
[03:55] Ari: Prefer private VPC for data residency, but for the POC we can do hosted if we put strict isolation and KMS.
[04:03] Tariq: We need audit logs and HSM-esque key control. SOC2 scope matters — we'll need to see your security pack.
[04:10] Jordan: Understood. We'll send the security bundle. Redwood Private can run in your VPC; Dedicated pools are an option later for consistent throughput. For POC we recommend hosted with VPC peering + customer-managed KMS or bring-your-own-key; it's quicker.

[04:28] Priya: Bench plan sketch: Week 0-1: data ingest + small smoke runs; Week 1-2: controlled bench runs — extraction on labeled corpus, translation evaluation on held-out bilingual pairs, chat latencies under synthetic load; Week 2-3: focused model tuning (prompt templates, temperature, quantization config) and reruns, then handoff. We'll aim for a 3-week POC.
[04:48] Lena: 3 weeks sounds okay. Can we have a canary rollout so we don't break production?
[04:53] Marta: Yeah — our runtime supports canary routes and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency SLOs are missed. We'll show the routing policy config.

[05:02] Jordan: Cost tradeoffs — smaller quantized models reduce token cost but may drop extraction F1 by 2-6 points depending on prompt engineering. Larger models raise per-token cost and may need batching to be economical. Any strict vendor cost cap?
[05:16] Ari: The $0.02 per session is a soft cap; we can tolerate spikes during business hours but need an average. If heavier models give +0.03 in F1 for critical fields, we can discuss hybrid routing.

[05:30] Samir: On infra, if you need to run Falcon 40B low-latency we may need dedicated GPU pools — do you support autoscaling and burst capacity?
[05:36] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated offers reserved capacity with autoscaling and burst options. For the POC hosted infra with smart routing and fallback will probably be fastest to stand up.

[05:45] Lena: About multilingual — for Japanese we saw generalist models struggle. Is it worth including a specialist translation model for JA in the bench?
[05:52] Priya: Absolutely. We'll include at least one translation specialist (we called it Polyglot-XL) in the bench and compare to generalists. We'll also test round-trip quality with your bilingual pairs.

[06:04] Ari: Any concerns about hallucination on contract extraction? we need high precision on money, dates, party names.
[06:10] Priya: Hallucinations often come from context windows and prompt ambiguity. We'll use structured output templates and strict validation rules — e.g., regex checks for dates, currency, and entity alignment as post-filter. Also run calibration tests and include a human-in-the-loop threshold.

[06:30] Jordan: Example bench metrics we'll capture: extraction F1/precision/recall by field, chat p50/p95 latency (cold & warm), tokens per session, cost per 1k tokens, translation BLEU / human eval notes, model size / GPU footprint. Anything else?
[06:44] Tariq: Add audit log fidelity and key rotation tests. Also retention and deletion verification.

[06:50] Priya: For the model shortlist we'll recommend an initial pairing: Llama3-13B-instruct (quantize to 4-bit) for extraction baseline, Mistral-7B-instruct for chat routing, Polyglot-XL for translation checks, and Falcon-40B-instruct as a high-quality fallback for tough extraction cases. We'll run those across your datasets and show where tradeoffs land.
[07:14] Ari: Sounds good. Can you estimate expected latency for each at our token sizes?
[07:18] Priya: Rough estimates: quantized 13B ~ p50 180-260ms for 175-token sessions on optimized GPUs; 7B models ~ 120-180ms; Falcon-40B depends — if sharded across 2-4 GPUs maybe 320-600ms p50 but better F1 for extraction. These are ballpark and we'll measure precisely.

[07:40] Lena: For prompts, we have in-house templates; can you test both our prompts and your recommended prompt-templates?
[07:45] Marta: Yes we'll run A/B with your prompts and our optimized instruction templates. Also we can test quantization knobs and their impact on F1.

[07:54] Jordan: Data privacy — for hosted bench do you want data redaction?
[07:58] Ari: We'll redact PHI and PII sketches, but supply enough realistic examples. Some contract samples must remain intact; we'll discuss redaction scope in the off-line doc.

[08:08] Tariq: On KMS: we need proof of BYOK integration and key lifecycle diagrams.
[08:12] Jordan: We'll send the security bundle — includes KMS options, SOC2 artifact summaries, SAML/SSO guides, and audit log examples.

[08:20] Priya: Any regulatory or residency constraints?
[08:23] Ari: EU data must stay in EU regions for EU customers; US data in US; POC can run in US but we need to confirm with privacy team.

[08:31] Jordan: Noted. We'll ensure region pinning in the bench.

[08:35] Samir: On benchmarking infra, can you provide the runner scripts and a reproducible harness? we prefer reproducibility so we can re-run after tuning.
[08:43] Priya: Yes — we'll hand over a dockerized harness plus a runbook with commands to reproduce. We'll also push logs and per-token cost breakdowns.

[08:52] Lena: Timeline recap? you suggested 3 weeks — can you map milestones?
[08:56] Jordan: Week 0 (this week): data exchange, security review. Week 1: smoke + bench runs. Week 2: tuning + reruns and earliest decisions. Week 3: final report and recommendations. We'll send a calendar invite for the bench kickoff on 10/12.

[09:14] Ari: Who will own the bench run?
[09:17] Priya: Priya and Marta will drive bench runs; Samir and Ari will verify infra and datasets. Jordan will coordinate deliverables.

[09:25] Jordan: Any blockers we should know?
[09:28] Tariq: SOC2 questions and KMS confirmations — otherwise ok.
[09:31] Samir: Access to the sample dataset and test accounts.

[09:35] Jordan: Great. Quick pricing note: we'll give an estimated cost sheet with model cost per 1k tokens for the shortlisted models and example session cost calculations. This is ballpark and will be refined after bench.

[09:46] Lena: One more ask — can you include a small decision matrix that shows where each model sits on latency vs extraction quality vs cost?
[09:52] Marta: Yes we'll include a visual matrix and a recommendation for a hybrid route: lightweight chat 7B front-door, 13B instruct for most extraction, fallback to 40B for flagged low-confidence cases.

[10:05] Jordan: OK let's recap next steps — Jordan send model shortlist + bench matrix by Friday 10/08; Priya provide harness and perf targets by 10/11; SparrowTech to send datasets by 10/09; schedule bench kickoff 10/12. Also Jordan will attach security pack. Anything else?
[10:26] Ari: that's it from me. Thanks.
[10:29] Tariq: Thanks all.
[10:31] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and invites. Bye.

Summary (auto): POC scoping call to define success metrics (latency, extraction F1, cost), workload sizing (tokens, steady/peak throughput), and an open-model shortlist (13B instruct, 7B Mistral, Falcon-40B, Polyglot translation specialist, distilled chat models). Bench plan proposed 3-week timeline, hosted-with-VPC-peering recommended for rapid POC, with Private/Dedicated options for later. Security items (SOC2/KMS/audit logs) flagged as blockers to resolve.

Referenced artifacts: "Sample dataset link (incoming from SparrowTech)", "Redwood security bundle (will be attached)", "Bench matrix template (to be sent)"

End of transcript.
